shots.text: In a Delhi summer, shade decides whether a street can be walked. {GreenCityAI|GreenCity AI} finds the heat, street by street, and tests the fix before anyone builds it.

chapter: A digital twin from open data
shots.text: This is Connaught Place, New Delhi, as a {3D|three-D} twin built from open data: {212|two hundred and twelve} buildings from OpenStreetMap, {936|nine hundred and thirty-six} trees from a satellite canopy map on AWS, and the true sun for the {15th|fifteenth} of May.

Every hour, we trace the sun onto every footpath. At {7 a.m.,|seven a.m.,} a third of the walkways are in shade. By noon, the sun is {79|seventy-nine} degrees high, and only {4 percent|four percent} are. The hex map shows where walkers have nowhere to hide.
Around it, we read a kilometre of the city, and every number wears a label: observed, computed, simulated or proposed.

Analyze scans Middle Circle at Radial Road {2.|two.} In simulated peak traffic, one approach carries {1.57|one point five seven} times its capacity, and at {3 p.m.,|three p.m.,} {85 percent|eighty-five percent} of the walkway nearby is in direct sun.
Claude Sonnet {5.5|five point five} is the street doctor. It answers only by calling our measuring tools, and a checker traces every number back to a tool.

Then we test fixes. Diverting some trips cuts the load from {1.57|one point five seven} to {1.44|one point four four} times capacity. {200|Two hundred} street trees lift day-long walkway shade from {13.9|thirteen point nine} to {17 percent.|seventeen percent.} Costs are labelled assumed, not quotes.
It works anywhere in India. Search for Charminar in Hyderabad, and the city map appears at once. Press build, and in under a minute, a new twin is ready.

Got a drone? Upload its point cloud, of any town or city. This public drone survey of the IIT Gandhinagar campus has {12.6 million|twelve point six million} points, and the file finds its own place on the map. The scan measures {71 of 73|seventy-one of seventy-three} buildings, and finds {2,380|two thousand three hundred and eighty} trees.
Every point here is real, shown as a photo, or by class: ground, roofs and trees, which we find ourselves, because drone surveys come without labels.
And the same scan as {3D|three-D} Gaussian splats: one splat for each measured point, drawn by our own WebGL renderer.
{GreenCityAI:|GreenCity AI:} open data and drone scans in, cooler streets out. Built with AWS Open Data and Claude. The code is on GitHub.
